Priya — thanks for the clarity. Short answer: yes, we can support split invoicing. Below are two viable approaches and the tradeoffs from Redwood's perspective: 

1) Split invoices at contract signing (recommended for procurement simplicity):
   - Issue Invoice A: Year 1 prepay (covers months 1-12) charged to FY26.
   - Issue Invoice B: Year 2 prepay (covers months 13-24) charged to FY27.
   - Each invoice would be recorded as deferred revenue on our books, then recognized monthly over the applicable 12-month coverage.

2) Single upfront invoice (what some customers prefer for admin simplicity):
   - One invoice for full 24-month prepay charged to FY26.
   - Redwood recognizes revenue monthly over 24 months.

Questions for you so we align:
- Will OrthoMed be providing a PO for Year 2 now, or will Lars/finance issue a second PO at the start of FY27? Either works; if you can provide a PO now and want the second invoice to be held until FY27, we can add a billing trigger date.

Rafael / team — see guidance below. I also attached a short note (revrec_guidance.pdf) that you can share with OrthoMed's finance folks.

Summary (two options):
A) Two annual prepay invoices (preferred for buyer):
   - Invoice 1 (covers months 1-12): record as Deferred Revenue (Liability). Recognize revenue monthly over months 1-12.
   - Invoice 2 (covers months 13-24): when paid, record as Deferred Revenue; recognize monthly over months 13-24.
   - Net effect on revenue recognition: same as straight-line per-month weightings for the period each invoice covers.

B) One upfront invoice for full 24 months:
   - Record full amount as Deferred Revenue; recognize evenly over 24 months.
   - Slightly simpler for our AR/AP but may cause buyer budget friction.

Practical items / wording for invoices:
- Invoice line item: "Redwood Inference — 24-month Platform Access (Period YYYY-MM-DD to YYYY-MM-DD) — Split Invoice (Year 1)"
- Include PO number field and Buyer GL code field (we will mirror the value in our AR notes).
- Add a note: "Payment constitutes prepayment for the indicated coverage period; revenue will be recognized monthly over service coverage period per Redwood Inference revenue policy."

GL / tax:
- Use deferred revenue liability account 2101 for prepayments.
- Tax: For US entities, sales tax usually not applicable for SaaS in many states; confirm with OrthoMed locale. If OrthoMed is paying from an EU entity, they should provide VAT registration for reverse charge (we will treat as zero-rated with documentation).

PO timing:
- If they provide PO for Year 2 now and request we not invoice until FY27, we can add a billing trigger date to Invoice B (we do not need the PO to be issued again). Alternatively, we can accept a placeholder PO and invoice later. Make sure the PO number is in the invoice/line-item for buyer accounting.

I recommend we share revrec_guidance.pdf with Priya/Lars and propose the split-invoice approach if it eases their internal approvals. Happy to join a call if they want to walk through with their finance team.
